finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can delete any account by ID (broken access control / IDOR). The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which shows the intended behavior.
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user sends DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id, including accounts owned by other users.
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at line 23, which deletes the account.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the entry point for DELETE /accounts/{id}; id is attacker-controlled.
The account is looked up by the attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter.
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored. No exception is thrown and no branch depends on it.

finding.guards_checked: canDelete at line 9 would block non-owners and non-admins, but its return value is dropped. assertCanDelete (line 13), which throws, is not used on this path. No other auth layer exists in the code. If a controller-level check exists outside this file, it was not visible. If the account does not exist, a is null and canDelete throws an NPE; that is only a robustness issue and not a guard.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (line 9) returns a boolean but its result is discarded at line 22; assertCanDelete (line 13) throws but is only used in closeAccount (line 29). No other guard exists in the code.
verdict.reason: src/AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete as a bare statement with the result discarded, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any caller. The ownership check is never enforced, unlike assertCanDelete at line 29 in closeAccount. A controller-level check outside this file could not be ruled out, but none exists in the available code.

verdict_facts.guard_found: canDelete (line 9) returns a boolean that is discarded at line 22; assertCanDelete (line 13) throws but is only used in closeAccount. No other control exists in the directory.
verdict_facts.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean from canDelete(u, a) is a bare statement whose result is ignored, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user and any existing account id.
